about.title: About Mus Manager
about.subtitle: Passion for tradition, precision for the game.
about.p1: Mus Manager was born from a need shared by thousands of fans: to professionalize the management of one of the most emblematic games of our culture. What started as an internal tool for small neighborhood clubs has become the leading platform for organizing Mus tournaments worldwide today. Our story begins at a small wooden table, between bids and 'órdagos', where we realized that the complexity of organizing a tournament —brackets, matchups, points, and tiebreakers— often took time away from what's truly important: enjoying the game and the company. We then decided to apply the latest technology to create an environment where tradition and modernity join hands in an elegant and robust way.
about.mission_text: Our mission is to preserve the essence of Mus by providing organizers with modern digital tools that eliminate the chaos of paper and spreadsheets. We want the players' only focus to be the game, the bid, and the strategy. We firmly believe that Mus is much more than just a card game; it is a social rite that fosters friendship and healthy competition. By digitizing management, we not only facilitate the organizer's work but also elevate the player's experience, allowing them to follow their progress in real-time, consult historical statistics, and feel part of a professional and passionate community.
about.why_text: Unlike other generic sports management tools, Mus Manager is specifically designed for the unique scenarios of Mus: zero management, club leagues with their particular rules, direct knockouts with traditional tiebreaker systems, and real-time standings adapted to each regulation. We don't try to adapt tennis or football software to cards; we've built this platform from scratch with the 'musolari' in mind. Our interface is clean, fast, and optimized for mobile devices, because we know a tournament is better lived with a smartphone in one hand and cards in the other. Furthermore, we maintain an unwavering commitment to being free for groups of friends and non-profit clubs.
about.tradition_text: We understand that Mus is a social rite, an excuse to gather and compete with nobility. That's why our platform is 100% free for social clubs and groups of friends, ensuring no one is left out of the digital table. At Mus Manager, we respect the history of the game, its gestures, its signs, and its unique language. Our technology doesn't replace the organizer but empowers them. We want the clubs that have been organizing tournaments on paper for decades to find in us a natural, simple, and satisfying transition. At the end of the day, what we seek is for Mus to remain alive, strong, and adapted to the 21st century, allowing new generations to discover the magic of this game with the tools that are already part of their daily lives.
about.vision_text: We aspire to become the global management standard for all mental sports and traditional board games. We want to create an interconnected network where players can have a unique profile, accumulate merits in different tournaments and federations, and where organizers can professionalize their events regardless of their scale. Technology should be a bridge, not a barrier, and Mus Manager is the first step toward a global, transparent, and technologically advanced Mus community.

how_it_works_page.title: Your Tournament, Step by Step
how_it_works_page.subtitle: Discover how easy it is to professionalize your Mus club.
how_it_works_page.intro: Organizing a Mus tournament shouldn't be a math exam. At Mus Manager, we've simplified the process so that anyone, regardless of their technical knowledge, can launch a successful event in minutes. Here we explain the path from registration to the podium.

step1.title: Community Setup
step1.desc: The first step is to create the home for your tournaments. A community can be your lifelong club, a bar, a gastronomic society, or simply your Thursday group of friends. By creating it, you can invite other organizers and start registering the player database that will regularly participate.

step2.title: Event Creation
step2.desc: Click on 'Create New Tournament' and fill in the basic details: name, date, location, and poster. The most important thing here is choosing the game system (league, knockout, groups, zeros) and defining the specific rules (points, sets, kings). Mus Manager will handle adapting all the tournament logic to these preferences.

step3.title: Registration and Draw
step3.desc: Add participating teams. You can do it manually or allow players to pre-register. Once you have all the brave ones, click the 'Generate Bracket' button. The system will perform the draw automatically, assigning tables and matchups in a fair and transparent way.

step4.title: Live Management
step4.desc: During the tournament, your main task will be entering results. After each match, find the corresponding table on your panel and note the score (e.g., 3-1). At that precise moment, the general standing is recalculated, and the knockout bracket advances. Players can consult this from their own mobiles by scanning the tournament's QR code.

step5.title: History and Statistics
step5.desc: When the tournament ends, the data is not lost. Mus Manager keeps a detailed history of all matches played, allowing you to consult who is the historical champion of your club or how many times a particular pair has won. Data is your community's legacy.

mus.q: What types of tournaments can I create?
mus.a: You can create three main competition formats: Direct Knockout (with an optional consolation bracket), League (round-robin) where you play regular matches, and the hybrid Group Stage + Final Stage format, ideal for fast but fair tournaments. We will be adding the traditional Ceros format soon.

mus.q: How many pairs can I register in a tournament?
mus.a: There is no strict limit imposed by the application. You can manage everything from small tournaments of 4 pairs to macro-events of more than 128 pairs. The system will automatically adapt the number of tables and rounds required based on the chosen format.

mus.q: Can I create a private tournament that only participants can see?
mus.a: Yes, absolutely! When creating or editing a tournament, you can check the "Privacy" option to make it private. This will prevent it from appearing in search engines and public listings on the website. Only people with the direct link you share will be able to access and view the results and pairings.

mus.q: How is the knockout bracket generated automatically?
mus.a: Once the participating pairs are confirmed in the Administration tab, if the format is Knockout, the system performs a fair random draw to pair the participants and arrange the play tables with a single click. If it's a hybrid format, the final bracket is automatically generated at the end of the group stage based on the official standings.

mus.q: Can I modify results once they have been entered?
mus.a: Yes, as the administrator and creator of the tournament, you have full freedom to correct any result at any time from the game administration section. The overall classification and subsequent matchups will be recalculated automatically and immediately upon saving the new score.

mus.q: What happens if there is an odd number of pairs in a league?
mus.a: The system is designed to handle odd numbers of teams intelligently. In each round, one of the pairs will automatically be assigned a "Rest" status. In the overall standings, matches played are balanced proportionally and cleanly without altering the official rules.

mgmt.q: Can I delegate the management of a tournament to someone else?
mgmt.a: Currently, management is linked to the account of the organizer who created the tournament. However, we are actively working on a co-administrator system to allow you to invite other registered users to enter results and configure tables from their own devices simultaneously.

mgmt.q: How do I share the tournament with participants?
mgmt.a: In your tournament dashboard, you will find a "Copy Link" button. You can send this web link via WhatsApp, Telegram, email, or social media. Participants can open it and see all rankings and matchups live without needing an account or installing anything.

mgmt.q: Can I add a poster or image to the tournament?
mgmt.a: Yes! During tournament creation or editing, you can upload a JPG or PNG image to act as the official poster. This image will appear prominently in the tournament header, in the participants' public view, and in the platform's general directory.

mgmt.q: Can participants see results in real time?
mgmt.a: Yes, the platform updates instantly. As soon as you save a table's result in your panel, any participant viewing the tournament's public view will immediately see the updated score, standings changes, and the next pairing.

mgmt.q: Can I export the tournament results?
mgmt.a: Currently, results and standings are permanently stored digitally so you can access them whenever you want. We are implementing a download option in PDF and spreadsheet (Excel) formats so organizers can archive or physically print the official standings.

account.q: Can I have multiple active tournaments at the same time?
account.a: Yes, there are no restrictions on the number of simultaneous tournaments you can manage. As an organizer, you can run multiple tournaments in parallel in the same venue or in different locations without any interference.

account.q: How do I delete my account and data?
account.a: We respect your privacy to the absolute fullest. If you wish to delete your account and permanently remove all associated information (including created tournaments), you can send us a formal request from your registered email to info@musmanager.com, and we will proceed with the immediate deletion.

Absolutely. All personal information and tournament records are transmitted via secure HTTPS encrypted connections and stored on cloud servers with industry-standard security protocols. We will never sell your data or share it with unauthorized third parties.

ads.q: Why is there advertising in the app?
ads.a: To keep Mus Manager as a free, accessible, and high-quality tool for the entire community of players without requiring subscription fees. Advertising revenue allows us to cover the costs of servers, databases, and technical development maintenance.

ads.q: Is the advertising targeted at minors?
ads.a: No. Mus Manager strictly complies with legal regulations regarding minor protection. We implement advanced advertising filters to prevent inappropriate content or ads targeted at minors, ensuring a safe and respectful browsing experience at all times.

ads.q: Can I use the app without seeing ads?
ads.a: Currently, full access to all organization and viewing tools is supported by ads to ensure they remain free. However, we are evaluating the possibility of introducing a premium ad-free subscription in the future for commercial venues or federations.

ads.q: Does Mus Manager intermediate with money, payments, or betting?
ads.a: No, not at all. Mus Manager is exclusively a sports and recreational management software to generate brackets, record match scores, and display standings. The platform does not process payments, does not collect entry fees, does not manage cash prizes, and does not allow financial betting of any kind.

reglas_page.title: Learn to Play and Organize Mus
reglas_page.subtitle: The ultimate guide on traditional Mus rules, advanced strategies, and professional tournament organizational systems.
reglas_page.rules_title: 1. Official Rules of Mus (4 Kings / 8 Kings)
reglas_page.rules_intro: Mus is a traditional Spanish deck card game with centuries of history. It is played by pairs (4 players in total) and stands out for its combination of strategy, psychology, discarding, and, above all, the art of bluffing.
reglas_page.rules_deck_text: A standard 40-card Spanish deck is used. In the most common variant (8 Kings, typical of Basque and Navarre Mus), Threes equal Kings (face cards) and Twos equal Aces. Thus, there are 8 Kings and 8 Aces in the deck. In the 4 Kings variant (typical of Castilian Mus), each card maintains its original nominal value and these equivalences are not used.
reglas_page.rules_rounds_intro: Each hand strictly consists of four independent betting rounds played in this exact order:
reglas_page.rules_round1_desc: Won by the pair with the highest face-value cards (Kings, Knights, Jacks...). The order is from highest to lowest.
reglas_page.rules_round2_desc: Won by the pair with the lowest face-value cards. The order is reversed (Aces, twos, threes...).
reglas_page.rules_round3_desc: Requires having at least two matching cards. There are three types: Simple pair (two matching cards), Medias (three matching cards), and Duples (four matching cards or two pairs of matching cards). Duples beats Medias, and Medias beats Simple pair. At equal rank, the highest card wins.
reglas_page.rules_round4_desc: Card values are added up (Face cards are worth 10, Aces are worth 1, other cards their face value). If the sum is 31 or more, players have 'Juego'. The best game is 31, followed by 40, 36, 35, 34, 33, and 32. If no one reaches 31, 'Punto' is played, and the pair closest to 30 wins.
reglas_page.rules_betting_text: In each lance, the first active player (mano) starts by saying 'Paso' (pass) or 'Envido' (putting 2 scoring points or counters at stake in the match). The opposing pair can 'Querer' (accept the point challenge), 'Pasar' (fold the round, yielding 1 point), or 'Reenvidar' (increase the points at stake). The ultimate bid is the 'Órdago', contesting all points of the entire set (chico). These points (amarracos) are strictly scoring units inherent to the card game rules and have no monetary value.
reglas_page.strategy_intro: Mus is a game of incomplete information where coordination with your partner and reading your opponents defines true champions.
reglas_page.strategy_card1_desc: Knowing when to ask for cards (mus) and when to cut (no mus) is vital. Being the first to speak (mano) is an immense tactical advantage. If you have a strong hand or want to disrupt the opponents' draw, declare 'No hay mus'. Selectively discarding helps your partner deduce your hand strength.
reglas_page.strategy_card2_desc: Bluffing (betting without matching pairs or game) is the heart of the game. A good bluffer studies the opponent's body language and betting patterns. Consistency is key: your bets must tell a believable story. Do not always bet on solid hands, nor bluff with no backup plan.
reglas_page.strategy_card3_desc: Mus allows transmitting information about your cards to your partner using official coded facial expressions. It is strictly forbidden to lie with signs, make false signs, or hide signs from opponents if they are looking directly at you. The official signs are: biting the lower lip (two kings), sticking out the tongue (two aces), winking (medias), raising eyebrows (duples), twisting the mouth (31 game), and shrugging (nothing/no pairs).
reglas_page.org_intro: Organizing a successful tournament requires mathematical rigor in pairings and a clear structure that players can easily understand.
reglas_page.org_card1_desc: The classic and most exciting format. Pairs are matched by draw and compete. To prolong play, many traditional tournaments use the 'Double Elimination' or 'Re-entry' (Consolation) system, where losing pairs enter a secondary bracket, giving them a second chance to reach the grand final.
reglas_page.org_card2_desc: Perfect for stable clubs and social groups with recurring meetings (weekly or monthly). All pairs play each other over several rounds. 3 points are awarded for a win, and 1 for a loss (or as per local rules). Tiebreaks are decided by overall set difference, and ultimately by the sum of points.
reglas_page.org_card3_desc: The perfect hybrid format for medium to large weekend tournaments. Pairs are divided into groups of 4 or 5. They play a quick round-robin, and the top 2 from each group advance to the knockout stage. Ensures everyone plays a minimum number of matches before elimination rounds.
reglas_page.rules_variant_text: Mus can be played with 4 Kings (original) or 8 Kings (Navarre/Basque Country). With 8 Kings, Threes are considered Kings, and Twos are considered Aces. It is crucial to define the variant before dealing!
